Name: Classic Margherita Pizza
Description: A timeless Italian pizza with fresh basil and mozzarella.
FullDescription: Originating from Naples, this pizza celebrates simplicity with quality ingredients and a blistered crust. The secret lies in using San Marzano tomatoes and fresh buffalo mozzarella for an authentic Neapolitan experience.
Steps: Preheat oven to 250 degrees C with a pizza stone if available.
Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface to about 30cm diameter.
Spread tomato sauce evenly, leaving a 2cm border for the crust.
Add torn mozzarella pieces over the sauce.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until the crust is golden and cheese is bubbling.
Remove from oven and top with fresh basil leaves.
Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil and serve immediately.

Name: Chicken Ramen Bowl
Description: Rich broth, tender chicken, and springy noodles.
FullDescription: A comforting Japanese-style ramen with a deeply savoury chicken broth, perfectly soft-boiled eggs, and classic toppings. The broth is the heart of this dish - patient simmering rewards you with incredible depth of flavour.
Steps: Simmer chicken stock with a thumb of ginger and 3 garlic cloves for 30 minutes.
Season broth with soy sauce, mirin, and sesame oil. Taste and adjust.
Cook noodles according to package instructions; drain and divide into bowls.
Pan-sear chicken thighs until golden, about 4 minutes per side. Rest then slice.
Soft-boil eggs for exactly 6.5 minutes; cool in ice water then peel.
Ladle hot broth over noodles, top with sliced chicken and halved eggs.
Garnish with spring onions, nori, and a drizzle of sesame oil.

Name: Street-Style Tacos
Description: Spiced beef tacos with lime, onion, and cilantro.
FullDescription: Inspired by Mexican street vendors - quick, bold flavours in every bite. The key is using fresh corn tortillas, properly seasoned meat, and simple but vibrant toppings. Less is more with street tacos.
Steps: Brown ground beef in a hot pan, breaking it apart as it cooks.
Season with cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Warm corn tortillas in a dry pan or directly over a gas flame until lightly charred.
Fill each tortilla with a scoop of seasoned beef.
Top with finely diced white onion and fresh cilantro leaves.
Squeeze lime juice over each taco and serve immediately.

Name: Berry Cheesecake
Description: Creamy no-bake cheesecake topped with mixed berries.
FullDescription: A light and luscious dessert perfect for summer gatherings - no oven required. The creamy filling sets beautifully in the fridge, and the berry topping provides a gorgeous pop of colour and freshness.
Steps: Crush digestive biscuits into fine crumbs using a food processor or rolling pin.
Mix crumbs with melted butter until combined. Press firmly into a 20cm springform tin.
Refrigerate the base for 20 minutes until firm.
Beat cream cheese with icing sugar and vanilla extract until completely smooth.
Fold in whipped double cream until just combined - do not overmix.
Spread filling over the chilled base and smooth the top.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight until set.
Top with fresh mixed berries before serving.

Name: Spaghetti Carbonara
Description: Silky egg sauce with crispy pancetta and pecorino.
FullDescription: The authentic Roman recipe - no cream, just technique and great ingredients. The secret is working quickly off the heat so the eggs form a silky sauce rather than scrambling. Proper carbonara is an art form.
Steps: Cook spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Render pancetta in a cold pan over medium heat until crispy.
Whisk egg yolks with most of the pecorino, a pinch of salt, and black pepper.
Remove pasta from heat; add to the pancetta pan with a splash of pasta water.
Away from heat, stir in egg mixture quickly, adding pasta water to create a silky sauce.
Serve immediately topped with remaining pecorino and extra black pepper.

Name: Pad Thai
Description: Thailand's iconic stir-fried noodle dish with peanuts and lime.
FullDescription: A perfectly balanced sweet, salty, sour, and umami stir-fry. The key is high heat and having all ingredients prepped before you start - pad thai cooks in minutes and cannot wait.
Steps: Soak rice noodles in cold water for 30 minutes; drain well.
Mix fish sauce, tamarind paste, and palm sugar for the sauce.
Heat wok over very high heat until smoking. Add oil.
Stir-fry prawns 2 minutes until pink; push to side.
Scramble eggs in the pan, then mix with prawns.
Add noodles and sauce; toss vigorously for 2 minutes.
Add bean sprouts, toss once more. Serve topped with crushed peanuts and lime.

Name: Classic Guacamole
Description: Fresh avocado dip with lime, chilli, and tomato.
FullDescription: The only guacamole recipe you'll ever need. Using perfectly ripe avocados and keeping it chunky is the way to go. Never use a food processor - guacamole should be roughly mashed with character.
Steps: Halve avocados, remove stones, and scoop flesh into a bowl.
Add lime juice immediately to prevent browning.
Mash with a fork until roughly chunky - not smooth.
Fold in jalapeno, red onion, tomatoes, and cilantro.
Season with salt and more lime if needed.
Serve immediately with tortilla chips.

Name: Butter Chicken
Description: Creamy tomato curry with tender spiced chicken.
FullDescription: A restaurant favourite made at home - marinated chicken simmered in a rich, buttery tomato sauce with warm spices. Serve with basmati rice or warm naan for a complete Indian feast.
Steps: Marinate chicken in yoghurt, half the garam masala, and salt for at least 30 minutes.
Sear chicken in a hot pan until golden; set aside.
Saute onion and garlic in butter until soft. Add tomato passata and simmer 10 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan; simmer 15 minutes until cooked through.
Stir in cream and remaining garam masala. Simmer 5 minutes until silky.
Garnish with coriander and serve with rice or naan.

Name: Classic Smash Burger
Description: Crispy-edged beef patty with cheese and pickles.
FullDescription: The secret to a great smash burger is a ripping-hot pan and thin patties pressed flat for maximum crust. Stack with melty cheese, tangy pickles, and a soft brioche bun.
Steps: Divide beef into 4 loose balls; season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a cast-iron pan until smoking. Place a ball on the pan and smash flat with a spatula.
Cook 2 minutes until deeply browned; flip, add cheese, and melt.
Toast buns cut-side down in the same pan.
Stack patty on bun with sauce, pickles, and onion. Serve immediately.

Name: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
Description: Light, stackable pancakes with maple syrup.
FullDescription: Weekend breakfast perfection - tall, tender pancakes with a slight tang from buttermilk. The batter should be lumpy; overmixing is the enemy of fluffiness.
Steps: Whisk flour, baking powder, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a large bowl.
Beat eggs into buttermilk; fold into dry ingredients with melted butter until just combined.
Rest batter 5 minutes while heating a lightly buttered non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake; cook until bubbles form, then flip.
Cook 1-2 minutes more until golden. Keep warm and repeat.
Serve stacked with butter and maple syrup.

Name: Korean Bibimbap
Description: Rice bowl with vegetables, egg, and gochujang.
FullDescription: A colourful Korean classic - warm rice topped with seasoned vegetables, marinated beef, a fried egg, and spicy gochujang sauce. Mix everything together before eating for the full experience.
Steps: Cook rice and keep warm. Season and saute beef until caramelised; set aside.
Blanch spinach; squeeze dry and toss with sesame oil and salt.
Stir-fry carrot and other vegetables separately until tender-crisp.
Fry eggs sunny-side up with runny yolks.
Arrange rice in bowls; top with beef, vegetables, egg, and gochujang.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve; mix at the table.

Name: Egg Fried Rice
Description: Wok-tossed rice with egg, peas, and soy sauce.
FullDescription: The best fried rice uses day-old chilled rice and fierce wok heat. Each grain should be separate and lightly smoky - a perfect way to use leftover rice.
Steps: Heat wok over highest heat until smoking. Add oil.
Scramble eggs quickly; break into pieces and push aside.
Add rice; toss and press against the wok to char slightly.
Add peas and soy sauce; toss vigorously 2-3 minutes.
Finish with spring onions and sesame oil. Serve immediately.

Name: Seafood Paella
Description: Saffron rice with prawns, mussels, and peppers.
FullDescription: Spain's most famous rice dish - socarrat, the crispy caramelised layer at the bottom, is the prize. Use a wide shallow pan and resist stirring once the stock is added.
Steps: Steep saffron in 2 tbsp warm stock. Saute onion and garlic in olive oil.
Add rice; stir 1 minute to coat. Add paprika and saffron stock.
Pour in hot stock; spread rice evenly. Do not stir from this point.
Simmer 15 minutes; nestle prawns, mussels, and pepper into the rice.
Cook 10 more minutes until rice is tender and socarrat forms at the base.
Cover with a towel 5 minutes; serve straight from the pan with lemon wedges.

Name: Salmon Poke Bowl
Description: Fresh salmon, avocado, and sushi rice bowl.
FullDescription: Hawaiian-inspired healthy bowl - cubed sashimi-grade salmon marinated briefly in soy and sesame, served over seasoned rice with creamy avocado and crunchy vegetables.
Steps: Cook sushi rice; season with rice vinegar and a pinch of sugar.
Toss salmon cubes with 1 tbsp soy sauce and sesame oil; chill 10 minutes.
Divide rice between bowls. Arrange salmon, avocado, and edamame on top.
Drizzle with remaining soy sauce and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Serve immediately while salmon is cold and fresh.

Name: Fudgy Chocolate Brownies
Description: Dense, gooey-centred brownies with crackly top.
FullDescription: The ultimate chocolate fix - a thin, crackly crust giving way to a fudgy, underbaked centre. Use good dark chocolate and do not overbake.
Steps: Melt chocolate and butter together; cool slightly.
Whisk in sugar, then eggs one at a time, then vanilla.
Fold in flour, cocoa, and a pinch of salt until just combined.
Pour into a lined 20cm square tin.
Bake at 180 degrees C for 25-28 minutes - centre should still wobble slightly.
Cool completely before cutting for clean squares.

Name: Kung Pao Chicken
Description: Spicy stir-fry with peanuts, chillies, and tender chicken.
FullDescription: A Sichuan classic balancing heat, sweetness, and crunch - diced chicken wok-fried with dried chillies, Sichuan peppercorn, and roasted peanuts. Best served with steamed rice.
Steps: Marinate chicken with soy sauce, shaoxing wine, and cornflour for 15 minutes.
Heat wok until smoking; stir-fry chicken until just cooked; remove.
Fry dried chillies and peppercorn in oil until fragrant; add garlic and ginger.
Return chicken; add sauce of soy, vinegar, sugar, and a splash of stock.
Toss in peanuts and spring onions; serve immediately over rice.

Name: Sweet and Sour Pork
Description: Crispy pork pieces in tangy glossy sauce.
FullDescription: Cantonese comfort food - twice-fried pork stays crisp while bell peppers and pineapple add colour and sweetness to the balanced sweet-and-sour glaze.
Steps: Coat pork in seasoned cornflour. Deep-fry at 180 degrees C until pale gold; drain.
Increase oil to 190 degrees C; fry pork again until crisp and deep golden.
Stir-fry peppers and pineapple briefly in a clean wok.
Add vinegar, ketchup, sugar, and a little water; simmer until glossy.
Toss pork through sauce; serve hot with steamed rice.

Name: Mapo Tofu
Description: Silken tofu in spicy bean paste and minced pork sauce.
FullDescription: Ma po dou fu - numbing, spicy, and deeply savoury. The key is doubanjiang (fermented chilli bean paste) and a sprinkle of Sichuan peppercorn powder at the end.
Steps: Blanch tofu cubes in salted water 2 minutes; drain gently.
Brown pork mince in oil; add garlic and doubanjiang; fry until fragrant.
Pour in stock; slide in tofu carefully. Simmer 8 minutes without stirring hard.
Thicken with cornflour slurry until sauce coats the tofu.
Finish with peppercorn powder and spring onions. Serve with rice.
